name: Yoani Sánchez
role: Founder and director of 14ymedio, Cuba's first independent digital newspaper
statusNote: Released November 5, 2026 after more than nine hours in State Security custody.
summary: Havana based journalist who became internationally known through her blog Generación Y in 2007 and co-founded 14ymedio in 2014 with her husband, Reinaldo Escobar. She sits on the board of the Inter American Press Association. Cuban State Security has repeatedly detained her or blocked her from leaving home in 2026, including to stop her attending a US diplomatic reception in January, and held her for more than nine hours on November 5.

background: Sánchez trained as a philologist and built an audience abroad by posting about daily life in Cuba when internet access on the island was rare. The government long denied her permission to travel and state media cast her as a foreign funded provocateur. Her outlet, 14ymedio, reports from inside the island with part of its staff. In 2026, as the fuel blockade deepened the crisis, State Security moved from occasional detentions to routine home confinement around sensitive dates and diplomatic events.
openQuestions: Whether any charge was filed after the November 5 detention

name: Henry Constantín
role: Director of La Hora de Cuba, an independent outlet in Camagüey
statusNote: Held since September 16, 2026 on a "disobedience" charge; his lawyer has not been given the case file.
summary: One of the best known independent journalists in central Cuba. He runs La Hora de Cuba from Camagüey and is the Inter American Press Association's regional vice president for Cuba on its press freedom commission. He was detained three times in January 2026 alone, and since September 16 he has been in pretrial detention, first at the Villa María Luisa State Security base. The US State Department and the US Embassy in Havana have called his detention unjust.

background: Constantín has reported from Camagüey for more than a decade and has been arrested repeatedly, often around court dates or when accompanying colleagues to police summons. Press groups describe a pattern of short detentions without warrants, travel restrictions inside Cuba and long periods without information to family. The current case is the longest: pretrial detention on a disobedience charge, with his lawyer reportedly unable to see the file and therefore unable to appeal.

name: Adelth Bonne Gamboa
role: Independent journalist and activist; host of "Gusaneando con Adelth" on CubaNet
statusNote: Diario de Cuba reported a violent arrest, threats, a fine and seized equipment. Whether he is still held was not confirmed in the sources reviewed.
summary: A Havana activist in his early thirties who hosts a CubaNet show on shortages, blackouts and the economy. State Security pressured him into publicly quitting CubaNet in late 2025, questioned him about his pay from the outlet, and in October 2026 threatened him with up to ten years in prison if he kept reporting. He returned to the show in late September 2026 and was violently arrested on November 2.

timeline.event: Detained with other activists after a State Security summons; artist Yulier P arrested while accompanying him.

background: Bonne Gamboa represents a newer generation of Cuban critics who built audiences on social media rather than in traditional dissident groups. His case follows a pattern press groups describe as the main silencing method in Cuba: pressure on family and income, forced public resignations from independent outlets, and threats of long sentences, rather than immediate trials.

name: Camila Acosta
role: Independent journalist; CubaNet reporter and correspondent for Spain's ABC
statusNote: Handcuffed and taken in a police vehicle in Havana on November 3, 2026; released that night.
summary: A Havana based reporter for CubaNet and the Spanish daily ABC, and one of the most frequently detained journalists on the island. She was arrested during the July 2021 protests, which drew a public demand for her release from Spain's foreign minister, and has since faced repeated detentions, home confinement and surveillance. On November 3, 2026 agents handcuffed her in the street, a day after her CubaNet colleague Adelth Bonne Gamboa was arrested.

name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
role: President of Brazil, reelected October 25, 2026 for a fourth term
summary: Brazil's president and founder of the Workers' Party (PT). He governed from 2003 to 2010 and again from 2023, and on October 25, 2026 came back from second place in the first round to beat Flávio Bolsonaro 51.8% to 48.2%, a margin of about 4.4 million votes. He was jailed for 580 days in the Car Wash corruption probe before the Supreme Court annulled his convictions in 2021 and found the trial judge biased.

background: A former metalworker and union leader, Lula built the Workers' Party into Brazil's main force on the left and left office in 2010 with very high approval. The Car Wash investigation then convicted him, kept him out of the 2018 race, and later collapsed in the courts after leaked messages showed coordination between the judge and prosecutors. Supporters see his record as persecution reversed; critics point to the corruption documented around his governments and say the annulments were procedural, not acquittals.

name: Flávio Bolsonaro
role: Brazilian senator; Liberal Party (PL) presidential nominee who lost the 2026 runoff
status: Left Brazil despite a travel ban
statusNote: Landed in Miami on October 28, 2026 after missing a Supreme Court deadline to surrender his passports, which police then canceled. He denies wrongdoing.
summary: Eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro and a senator for Rio de Janeiro. He won the first round of the 2026 election but lost the runoff to Lula 48.2% to 51.8% and sought annulment. The next day a Supreme Court justice ordered him to hand over his passports in a money laundering probe tied to his lawyer friend Willer Tomaz and online betting firms; he missed the deadline and flew to Miami via Argentina. A separate inquiry looks at financing of a film about his father linked to the former owner of Banco Master.

background: Flávio inherited his father's movement after Jair was jailed and came close to winning the presidency. The 2026 inquiries are newer and sealed, so the public record is thin; he says they are political intimidation timed to his defeat. name: Jair Bolsonaro
role: Former president of Brazil (2019 to 2022), serving 27 years for a coup plot
statusNote: Moved from prison to house arrest in March 2026 after bronchopneumonia; the Supreme Court kept him there in July.
summary: Brazil's far right former president, sentenced in September 2025 to 27 years and 3 months for plotting to stay in power after losing to Lula in 2022, and barred from public office. He began serving in November 2025 after tampering with his ankle monitor, and has been under humanitarian house arrest since March 2026. His son Flávio carried his movement into the 2026 election and lost.
